expJobArr.expJobNote:
During my summer internship at TSMC Fab 18B, I participated in a yield improvement project for the dry etching process. At the time, an advanced process node encountered a yield bottleneck during a critical etching stage, requiring us to identify the root cause and propose process optimization solutions.


- Summer Internship Objective:


My primary responsibility was to assist the team in pinpointing bottleneck stations through data analytics, as well as analyzing plasma etching mechanisms and optimizing process parameters. The ultimate goal was to improve Critical Dimension (CD) uniformity and boost overall wafer yield.


- Identifying Bottlenecks: By analyzing historical SPC data and wafer defect maps, we discovered that yield failures were predominantly concentrated at the wafer edge and highly correlated with dry-etching depth fluctuations in specific equipment chambers.


- Root Cause Analysis: Over-etching penetrates the underlying stop layer, damaging the sub-surface device structures; conversely, under-etching leaves residual material, causing bridging defects. We concluded that the main issues stemmed from excessive ion bombardment caused by high bias power, alongside uneven plasma density distribution across the wafer edge.


- Numerical Analysis and Optimization: Through systematic Design of Experiments (DoE), we collaborated with the R&D team to fine-tune the bias power, reactant gas ratios, and chamber pressure. This effectively mitigated the microloading effect and achieved precise control over plasma etch depth and profile angles.
